title: This Is the Army takes its last bow
photoNote: Irving Berlin, in his First World War uniform, backstage with soldiers at This Is the Army. U.S. Army Signal Corps photo 111-SC-279543, public domain. Taken during the show's run, not at the final performance.
body:
Irving Berlin wrote a show for soldiers, starring soldiers, and took it from Broadway all the way to the Pacific. On this day it played for the last time.

22 October 1945. This Is the Army gave its final performance in Hawaii. Berlin stepped out and sang "Oh! How I Hate to Get Up in the Morning," the song from his own 1918 Army show, Yip Yip Yaphank.

The show had opened on Broadway on 4 July 1942 with a cast of 300 soldiers. Its proceeds went to Army Emergency Relief.

Berlin insisted on including Black soldiers, and the company was described as the only fully integrated outfit in the U.S. Army, except on stage.
threads:
Irving Berlin's soldier show This Is the Army gave its final performance on 22 October 1945, in Hawaii.

It had opened on Broadway on 4 July 1942 with 300 soldiers in the cast, and its proceeds went to Army Emergency Relief.

At the last show, Berlin himself sang "Oh! How I Hate to Get Up in the Morning."

sources.title: Today in World War II History, Oct. 22, 1940 and 1945, Sarah Sundin

photoCredit: Irving Berlin, in his First World War uniform, backstage with soldiers at This Is the Army, about 1943. U.S. Army Signal Corps 111-SC-279543, public domain.

declassified.fact: The 1943 Warner Bros. film of the show starred Lt. Ronald Reagan, the future president, and Sgt. Joe Louis, the heavyweight boxing champion, appeared as himself. Ray Heindorf's musical score won the film an Academy Award.
